items.text: As @POTUS mentioned during last night's #SOTU, we're working to end cancer as we know it. With the #CancerMoonshot we will cut the cancer death rate by 50%, support patients and families, and address disparities in cancer outcomes: https://t.co/ws2DJxOi2S https://t.co/DXMTFWiSf4

This Wednesday, the @WhiteHouse will be hosting a #CancerMoonshot Goals Forum to hear from patients and patient advocates about improving patient experiences in the diagnosis and treatment of cancer.  https://t.co/94uK5He4uf

A priority of the Biden-Harris Administration is to have the tools to test, treat, & prevent COVID. Point-of-care diagnostics & treatment sites, called for in @WHOSTP’s preparedness plan, are opening to prevent serious illness, keep people out of the hospital, and save lives.

The #CancerMoonshot is committed to ensuring that ALL cancer patients have access to high quality, equitable care. Yesterday’s announcement from @HHSGov & @CMSGov of a new model to improve cancer care for Medicare patients and lower healthcare costs, helps accelerate these goals.

The @USPTO extended its patent program to fast-track innovations in cancer treatment, cutting in half the time it takes to review cancer immunotherapy patent applications
https://t.co/cFUo0voszA

.@CMSGov launched its Enhancing Oncology Model, offering a new way to support Medicare cancer patients and their loved ones as they navigate the challenges of of facing cancer.
https://t.co/2qHJZ5lUd4

Tomorrow, OSTP and @NIMHgov will be hosting a conversation about the ways in which science has offered hope to treatment-resistant depression. This ongoing effort to combat the #MentalHealth crisis  is a major pillar of @POTUS' #UnityAgenda.

👩‍⚕️ The @WHCOVIDResponse team has emphasized rapid diagnosis and early treatment with anti-viral medication as a cornerstone of the USG pandemic response, launching the “test-to-treat” initiative.

🏥 Before the COVID-19 pandemic, only 187 healthcare facilities were able to use electronic case reporting for COVID-19 reports. As of July 7, 13,800+ healthcare facilities in 49 states can send COVID-19 eCRs.
